sentences.text: Dorea is a genus of Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming rod-shaped bacteria first isolated from human faeces.
By 16S rRNA sequence the genus sits in the Clostridium coccoides group, now usually treated as the family Lachnospiraceae.
Its nearest named relative at description was Eubacterium formicigenerans, from which the new faecal isolates were biochemically distinct.
A study of colorectal cancer tissue reported Dorea formicigenerans and other Lachnospiraceae enriched in normal colon tissue rather than in tumour tissue.
A 16S sequencing study of Parkinson's disease patients reported reduced Dorea content compared with healthy volunteers.
